stem:
Deepa looks at the diagram. Straight lines $EF$ and $GH$ cross at $N$. The marked angle $\angle ENG$ is $58^{\circ}$, and $q$ labels the angle vertically opposite $\angle ENG$.

Which two claims are correct?

One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Vertically opposite angles at the same crossing are equal.
Adjacent angles on a straight line are equal.

teacher.key_rationale: Vertically opposite angles at one crossing are equal, so q = 58°. Taking 122° uses an adjacent straight-line angle and omits the opposite-pair condition. Saying adjacent angles on a straight line are equal substitutes a different relation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle as crossing lines EF and GH at N with marked vertically opposite pair 58° and q.
